You asked for concrete examples and how to keep the guide price compliant without looking overly algorithmic. Below are pasteable copy blocks, wireframes-in-text, price-band logic, and a GA4 event map you can brief straight to devs.

Copy blocks (use as-is)
- Pre-form fee banner (visible before any field):
  "Sales: from 1.0% + VAT (no sale, no fee) • Lettings: Tenant-find from 8% + VAT • Fully managed from 12% + VAT"
- H1: "Get your free valuation"
- Progress labels: "Step 1 of 2: Your property" → "Step 2 of 2: Your details"
- Primary CTA (end of Step 1): "See your guide price now"
- Price panel header: "Your guide price"
- Price disclosure: "Guide only. Not a formal valuation. For an accurate price, book a free in‑person appraisal."
- Proof line under Step‑1 CTA: "Trusted by 3,200+ local sellers and landlords • 4.7★ Reviews"
- Secondary option (lighter): "Prefer to talk? 01926 555 210" and link: "Request a call today"

Wireframes (annotated)
Step 1 • Your property
[Progress: Step 1 of 2]
H1
Fee banner (full‑width, subtle)
Fields: Postcode → Address lookup • Property type • Bedrooms • Intent (Sell/Let)
Primary CTA: See your guide price now
Small proof directly below CTA (one line)
Secondary (text link): Prefer to talk? … • Request a call today

Step 2 • Your details
[Progress: Step 2 of 2]
Sticky price panel at top:
  Your guide price for [Town]
  £[min]–£[max]   Confidence: [High|Medium|Low]  (link: How we estimate)
  Guide only. Not a formal valuation…  (fees reminder line, light)
Form: First name • Last name • Email • Mobile • Timeframe • Consent (next to phone: "Tick if you’d like a call")
Primary CTA: Book your free in‑person appraisal
Secondary (text link): No thanks — email me the summary

On‑page price logic (keeps it indicative, not deterministic)
- Show a range band (e.g., £[min]–£[max]) rather than a single figure; avoid decimals.
- Use a simple confidence label (High/Medium/Low) tied to depth of recent local comparables; explain via a "How we estimate" note in plain English.
- Keep the guide price visible in Step 2 so the promise remains clear while details are completed.
- Reduce scraping/PII risk by showing only town or area with the price (e.g., "Your property in [Town]") and not the full address near the figure.
- Keep your fee info visible pre‑form (banner) and lightly reiterated near the price panel.

"How we estimate" microcopy (pasteable)
"We combine recent local sales and your property details to suggest a guide price. It’s indicative, not a valuation. A local valuer will confirm in person and can adjust up or down."

GA4 event map (names + triggers; no PII)
- valuation_start — on first interaction with a Step‑1 field (focus/change). params: intent, page_location, device.
- fee_banner_viewed — once when the banner enters viewport on Step 1. params: banner_version.
- see_price_click — on Step‑1 primary CTA click. params: intent, property_type, bedrooms.
- guide_price_shown — when the price panel renders (DOM visible after Step 1). params: price_band (e.g., "250k-300k"), confidence ("high|medium|low"), intent.
- details_submit — on Step‑2 submit (before network). params: appointment_preference ("visit|phone|email_summary").
- callback_requested — on "Request a call today". params: intent.
- outbound_call_click — on tel link click. params: intent.
- appraisal_booked — on booking confirmation. params: appointment_type ("in‑person|phone"), booking_lead_time_days.
Implementation note: fire events off user actions/DOM updates (dataLayer.push) to avoid extra network time; keep all PII (name, email, phone, full address) in your CRM, not GA4.
